records.statement: Overdispersed count data can be modeled with either quasi-Poisson or negative-binomial regression; the two approaches can produce materially different covariate-effect estimates.

The quasi-Poisson variance is a linear function of the mean, whereas the negative-binomial variance is a quadratic function of the mean; these different variance relationships change observation weights and can affect fitted covariate effects.
For Poisson data the variance equals the mean; count data with variance exceeding the mean are overdispersed and require reconsideration of ordinary Poisson assumptions.
